Create package infrastructure

A startup message

use_zzz() creates a package documentation file with .onLoad, .onAttach, and %||%. It is similar to usethis::use_package_doc() while also providing a useful starting template.

use_zzz(path = dir, open = FALSE)
#> ✔ Setting active project to "/tmp/RtmpUlamDe".
#> ✔ Created /tmp/RtmpUlamDe/R/RtmpUlamDe-package.R from template.
#> ✔ Adding cli to Imports field in DESCRIPTION.
#> 
#> ☐ Refer to functions with `cli::fun()`.

Check missing function in _pkgdown reference

check_pkgdown_reference() identifies exported functions that are absent from the reference section of _pkgdown.yml.

check_pkgdown_reference(pkg = dir)

Configure the clangd language server

use_clangd() writes a .clangd configuration file that lets the clangd language server find the system R headers and the include/ directory of the packages you pass in include (Rcpp, RcppEigen and RcppArmadillo by default). Packages that are not installed are skipped with a warning.

use_clangd(path = dir, overwrite = TRUE)
#> Warning: Package RcppEigen is not installed; skipping its
#> include path.
#> Warning: Package RcppArmadillo is not installed; skipping its
#> include path.
#> ✔ Created /tmp/RtmpUlamDe/.clangd.

When path is a package root, the file also disables background indexing for the R/ directory (which holds no C++ code) and adds .clangd to .Rbuildignore.

use_clangd(path = dir, include = c("Rcpp", "BH"), overwrite = TRUE)

Vendor permissively licensed code

use_vendor() records attribution and licensing information when incorporating selected source files from a permissively licensed GitHub R package. It creates an inst/vendor/ directory, a R/vendor-*.R file, and updates relevant DESCRIPTION fields.

try(use_vendor(
  pkg = "WangLabCSU/rpkgkit",
  "43_use_vendor.R",
  branch = "main",
  path = dir
))
#> ℹ Fetching repository information for WangLabCSU/rpkgkit...
#> ✔ Vendor package uses MIT license.
#> ✔ Created directory /tmp/RtmpUlamDe/inst/vendor/rpkgkit.
#> ✔ Copied LICENSE.
#> ✔ Copied LICENSE.md.
#> ✔ Created inst/vendor/rpkgkit/README.md.
#> ✔ Created /tmp/RtmpUlamDe/R/vendor-rpkgkit.R.
#> ✔ Added rpkgkit authors to Authors@R.
#> ✔ Updated DESCRIPTION.
#> ☐ Consider pasting the following statement into README.md
#> 
#> 
#> ## Acknowledgements
#> 
#> We would like to thank the following people and projects:
#> 
#> - The authors of the [rpkgkit](https://github.com/WangLabCSU/rpkgkit) package &mdash; **Yuxi Yang** &mdash; whose code is included (under MIT license) in `R/vendor-rpkgkit.R`.

Only packages with a supported permissive license can be vendored. Review the acknowledgement text printed by the function and add it to your README when appropriate.

rpkgkit::PERMISSIVE_LICENSE
#> [1] "MIT"          "Apache-2.0"   "Apache 2.0"   "BSD-2-Clause" "BSD-3-Clause"
#> [6] "Unlicense"    "CC0-1.0"      "CC0"

usethis extensions

Use the following helpers from the package root:

Use R 4.1.0 version

R 4.1.0 introduced the pipe (|>) and anonymous function \(). If these syntaxes need to be used in a package, the R package must require at least R version 4.1.0.

use_r_v4.1.0(path = dir)
#> ✔ Adding R to Depends field in DESCRIPTION.

Add URL in DESCRIPTION 

use_url(dir)

Add bug reports URL in DESCRIPTION 

use_bugreports(dir)

Open CFF

CITATION.cff files are plain text files with human- and machine-readable citation information for software and datasets.

Code developers can include such files in their source code repositories to let others know how to correctly cite their software.

open_cffinit()

This cannot replace usethis::use_citation(), it just complements project.

Global ignore-file templates

Use add_global_rbuildignore() and add_global_gitgnore() to add the corresponding global ignore-file templates to a package.

add_global_rbuildignore(path = dir)
#> ✔ Added 39 pattern(s) to .Rbuildignore.
add_global_gitgnore(pkg = dir)

Check system dependencies

Some packages need system development libraries (graphics and font libraries, for example) to compile. check_sysdeps() detects the package manager in use (dpkg, rpm, pacman, apk or brew), checks each dependency with it, and reports every hit and miss together with a ready-to-paste install command for the missing ones.

check_sysdeps()

With deps = NULL (the default), a built-in list of graphics and font libraries (freetype, libjpeg, libpng, libtiff, libwebp, harfbuzz, fribidi, fontconfig) is checked using the names that the detected package manager expects. Pass your own names in deps, and optionally set manager to check against a manager other than the detected one:

check_sysdeps(c("freetype-devel", "libwebp-devel"), manager = "rpm")

The result is returned invisibly as a named logical vector, so it can be reused in scripts. Set verbose = FALSE to keep the run silent:

ok <- check_sysdeps(verbose = FALSE)
ok[!ok]

Detect the Positron version

get_positron_version() reports the version of the Positron IDE that hosts the current R session. It is useful for diagnostics, bug reports, or for enabling IDE-specific behaviour only on recent builds.

get_positron_version() # e.g. "2025.01.0"
get_positron_version(long = TRUE) # e.g. "2025.01.0-123"

The version is looked up in three steps, in this order:

  1. the POSITRON_VERSION environment variable set by Positron for its R sessions (POSITRON_LONG_VERSION, which also carries the build number, when long = TRUE);
  2. the .ps.positron_version() helper that the IDE injects into the session;
  3. the positron --version command-line tool.

If the session does not run inside Positron and no positron executable is on PATH, the function returns NA_character_ instead of throwing an error, so it is safe to call in any session, including CI.
